title: Fractions: Equal Shares, Equivalent Fractions and Adding Fractions
seo_title: Fractions Class 6 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 7)
standard_text: Fractions as equal shares and parts of a collection, fractions on the number line, mixed numbers, equivalent fractions, comparing fractions and adding and subtracting fractions (summary of NCERT Ganita Prakash Class 6)
meta_desc: Class 6 Fractions worksheet (Ganita Prakash Chapter 7): equal shares, fraction of a quantity, mixed numbers, equivalent fractions, comparing, adding and subtracting fractions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Multiply or divide the top and bottom by the same number
key_sub: To add fractions, first make the denominators the same.
body_html:
How it works

A fraction like 3/4 means 3 of 4 equal parts. 3/4 of 20 = 20 ÷ 4 × 3 = 15.

Equivalent fractions come from multiplying or dividing top and bottom by the same number: 2/3 = 8/12. Lowest terms: 12/18 = 2/3.

To compare or add, use a common denominator: 1/4 + 2/3 = 3/12 + 8/12 = 11/12.

Example

Find 2/5 of 35.

35 ÷ 5 = 7

7 × 2

Answer: 14

Example

Add 1/2 + 1/3.

3/6 + 2/6

Answer: 5/6

Common mistakes

  • Adding the denominators: 1/2 + 1/3 = 2/5 is wrong.
  • Thinking 1/8 is bigger than 1/5 because 8 is bigger than 5.
  • Multiplying only the top to make an equivalent fraction.

faq.a: Fractions that name the same amount, such as 1/2, 2/4 and 3/6.

faq.q: How do you compare two fractions?
faq.a: Write them with the same denominator and compare the numerators.

faq.q: How do you add fractions with different denominators?
faq.a: Rewrite them with a common denominator, then add the numerators.
